corrections.severity: Incorrect peripheral mathematical assertion; excluded from disposition
corrections.claim: For trees inverse gap is within a constant factor of max_e R_e s_e(1-s_e/M).
corrections.correction: False for general trees. Unit-resistance n-edge path with original-degree masses has M=2n. For f(i)=i, mean=n/2, energy=n, and variance=n(n^2+2)/6. Thus tau >= (n^2+2)/6, while each bridge t_e<=n/2. The ratio is unbounded. Tree Hardy bounds require accumulated path/cut information; the exact rank-one bridge decomposition remains valid. Full F obtains comparison using probabilistic localization, not a universal tree inequality.

The claimed verbatim transfer to any block-decorated finite-variance GW map family is not independently proved here. Block connectivity, marking, conditioning lattice, and mass identities must be stated and verified. Do not record it as a new general theorem.

Title/abstract-level similarities are context, not exact theorem-level reductions. The contribution disposition relies on the explicit Janson hypothesis reduction, directly inspected Fill-Janson statements, and the elementary operations, not an asserted direct Flegel or random-matrix theorem implying F.

Do not infer the critical endpoint alpha=1/2 has the same macroscopic-branch limit as alpha>1/2. Fill-Janson Theorem 1.7(iv) has n log n leading expectation at the endpoint; any new spectral target needs separate normalization and proof.
